title: Design an Idempotent Playbook
objective: Structure plays, tasks, variables, pre-tasks, and handlers for repeatable configuration.

sourceAlignment.title: Ansible for DevOps, 2nd Edition
sourceAlignment.author: Jeff Geerling
sourceAlignment.note: Original companion material synthesizing the chapter's Node.js, LAMP, and Solr examples.

paragraphs: A playbook turns isolated operations into a reviewed sequence. Each play selects hosts and contains ordered tasks; modules keep package installation, configuration lines, services, repositories, and application deployment idempotent.
Variables separate environment-specific values from procedure. Pre-tasks prepare prerequisites, normal tasks converge the system, and handlers defer service restarts until a notifying change occurs.

Use --limit to reduce scope, --check and --diff to preview, and explicit become settings for privileged work. Complex application stacks should remain understandable from task names and module choices.
explanation.rule: Describe desired state with named tasks, and restart services only when configuration changes.

examples.title: Notify a Handler
examples.code:
- name: Configure web servers
  hosts: webservers
  tasks:
    - name: Install nginx
      ansible.builtin.package:
        name: nginx
        state: present
      notify: Restart nginx
  handlers:
    - name: Restart nginx
      ansible.builtin.service:
        name: nginx
        state: restarted
examples.note: The handler runs at the end only when notified by a changed task.

checks.question: Why use a handler for a service restart?
options: It runs only when notified by a change

feedback.incorrect: Handlers avoid unnecessary restarts by responding to changes.

checks.question: A play fails with “No package matching ngnix is available.” What is the most direct fix?
options: Correct the package name to nginx and rerun

feedback.correct: Correct—fix the invalid desired state, then rerun the idempotent play.
feedback.incorrect: Do not hide the failure. Correct the misspelled package name and rerun.

assignment.title: Install and Start Nginx
assignment.brief: Write a webservers play that installs nginx and ensures it is started and enabled.
requirements: Set the service started and enabled.
The play must use become: true for package and service changes.
The play must use become: true for package and service changes.
The play must use become: true for package and service changes.
assignment.starterCode:
- name: Configure web servers
  hosts: webservers
  tasks:
assignment.solutionCode:
- name: Configure web servers
  hosts: webservers
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: Install nginx
      ansible.builtin.package:
        name: nginx
        state: present
    - name: Start nginx
      ansible.builtin.service:
        name: nginx
        state: started
        enabled: true
assignment.outputCheckLabel: Playbook uses valid course-style YAML structure

hints: Use separate package and service tasks.

lab.title: Mission: converge a web tier
lab.setup: Complete the playbook in the editor, copy it to /workspace/webservers.yml, then use the Terminal tab.
steps: Preview the play with ansible-playbook --check --diff webservers.yml.
Run the play normally and verify nginx starts on both webservers.
Run it again and require changed=0 in the play recap.
Temporarily misspell the package name, read the failure, then restore it.
lab.verify: ansible-playbook webservers.yml && ansible-playbook webservers.yml && ansible webservers -b -m ansible.builtin.service -a "name=nginx state=started"
lab.success: The second playbook run reports changed=0 and nginx is started on web01 and web02.
